result:
All 24 months are played and all three training runs were met with no penalties and no unserved inference. **Net cost: $1,057.5M.**

| Window | Done / needed |
|---|---|
| Months 0–7 | 135.5 / 60 |
| Months 8–15 | 209.0 / 140 |
| Months 16–23 | ~342 / 320 |

**Settlement:** spend $1,273.8M (equipment $849M, power $221M, cloud contracts $284M, spot $15M, interest $24M, resales −$120M), minus $330.9M for GPUs still held at month 24, plus $114.6M of contract and power payments due after month 23.

**How it went:**
- **Months 0–1:** supply looked tight. I contracted 25 MW of power, because 16 MW couldn't run all the GPUs already owned or in the queue. I also queued 12k gen H early and reserved two 3 kH, 24-month cloud contracts while prices were low.
- **Gen N launch:** I narrowed the launch to month 14 by combining the rumours (~12, ~12, ~15) with the missing month-12 confirmation, and it launched in month 14. Supply had turned loose, so the 10k gen N vendor order shipped by month 18. That plus a 5 kH reservation and one month of spot carried the last window.
- **Brokers:** I tested them before relying on them, which helped. Both gen N broker orders (B 4k, A 2k) were still cancelled at launch, costing about 20% of $288M (≈$58M). After that I stopped using brokers.

**What cost the most:**
- **Too much capacity in windows 1 and 2:** about 145 kH-months beyond what the runs needed, mostly early gen H and the two 24-month reservations. Ordering about 4–6k fewer gen H in month 0 would have been the biggest saving.
- **Over-contracted power:** I signed 45 MW in months 5–7 and peaked at 86 MW. Part of that was never used, and payments due after month 23 added to the $114.6M settled at the end.
- **The cancelled broker orders**, at about $58M.

The belief notes are in the log for each month. Some notes were cut short when a semicolon inside the text was read as the start of a new command. The notes still saved, and only the stray fragments errored out.
